segments.text: That to which the Scripture ascribes both impotency and enmity with respect to grace, cannot actively and of it self concurr to the production of it: But the Scripture ascribes both impotency and enmity to Nature with respect to grace. It denyes to it a power to do anything of it self, Joh. 15. 5. and which is less, it denies to it power to speak a good word, Matth. 12. 34. and which is least of all, it denies it power to think a good thought, 2 Cor. 3. 5. This impotency if there were no more, cuts off all pretence of our active concurrence, but then if we consider that it ascribes enmity to our natures as well as impotency, how clear is the case! see Rom. 8. 7. the carnal mind is enmity against God: and Col. 1. 21. and you that were enemies in your minds by wicked works. So then Nature is so far productive of this principle, as impotency and enmity can enable it to be so.
